Below the text, a horizontal rule, then the chapter heading, a italic title, and the opening paragraph with a drop cap. A catchword "rum" sits at the right below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: exprimatur, parens aut filius, verum tantum frater, amicus, proximus; attamen ex alio loco Scripturæ satis colligitur, Mosem etiam nominasse parentes & liberos; aut saltem Levitas mandatum Dei de occidendis vitiuli[?] cultoribus rectè ex pio zelo ita fuisse interpretatos, ut etiam parentes & liberos complecteretur. Ut jure divino filium à patre, & patrem à filio occidi posse, aliquo in casu haud illicitum judicari debeat.
main_text.head: CAP. XIII.

head.i: De Duellis feriis extra judicia gloria causâ susceptis.

main_text.p: FUit olim, & etiamnum est, populorum circa mores & instituta dissensus; quorum alii sese aliis in bello exercitatiores autumabunt, alii morum

page.notes: The drop cap "F" is joined to "Uit" as "FUit". The word "vitiuli" is printed as "viriuli" in the scan; it is transcribed as the likely intended word and marked [?]. The paragraph ends "alii mo-" with the printed hyphen, and "rum" is the catchword at the foot. A small speck between "tantum" and "frater" is ignored. Hyphen in the title "glo-ria" is printed at the line end and joined here.
